identity.life_stage: married, three grown children, cotton farmer

engagement.interaction_backstory: He runs a Saturday men's breakfast that forty farmers actually attend, and he plays music through the fellowship hall speakers while they eat. His congregation sings a cappella, so nothing from this site can ever be used in a service — but the breakfast is not a service, and that distinction is the whole reason he is here.

depth.core_contradiction: Belongs to a tradition that sings without instruments and has driven eleven hours to a bluegrass festival twice.
depth.wound: He lost the family land in 2014 and now farms ground his father used to own.
depth.faith_journey: Church of Christ, fifth generation, a cappella and no piano ever; he does not question it and he does not defend it either.
depth.voice_fingerprint: Long pauses. "Well." Says the important thing last and quietly.
depth.open_doubt: Whether the rules he was raised in are scripture or just West Texas.

social_graph.note: runs the books and the bible class; sharper than he is
a friend, and the man who holds the note

depth.emotional_weather_default: Steady; grim in a dry year and this is a dry year.
depth.daily_texture: 4:30am, the pivot, the co-op, the price board, forty men and a griddle on Saturdays.
depth.sensory_anchor: Four-part harmony with no instruments in a small hot building, and his grandfather's bass line.
depth.living_arc: One bad season from selling, and he has not told his wife how close it is.
